key_idea: Each wall removal merges exactly two faces, so the answer is the number of enclosed faces; count them by splitting every cell into four triangles and running DSU/flood fill.
sketch: Split every cell into top/right/bottom/left triangles. A '/' joins top with left and right with bottom, a backslash joins top with right and bottom with left, a '.' joins all four. Neighbouring cells share the facing triangles, and triangles on the border of the grid are joined to a virtual outside node. The number of DSU components minus one (the outside) is the number of enclosed regions, and since the face-adjacency graph is connected and each removed wall merges two faces, that is the minimum number of removals. O(RC alpha) on 4e6 nodes, well within 6 s. Pitfalls: diagonal walls do not block in a plain cell grid so a naive flood fill fails; reading backslashes correctly; memory for 4*R*C nodes.
